paper.title: Learning Loss for Active Learning
paper.brief_method_paraphrase: Joint task/loss training uses current hidden features and current annotated losses. Pairwise ranking addresses changing loss scale. Experiments obtain human labels; diversity is a stated limitation. These results do not establish noisy-teacher RMOT performance.
paper.retrieval: CVF PDF open returned403; arXiv primary full PDF/HTML method sections were read successfully. No third-party summary or code was used.

current_interface_observations: R consumes the9352D action features separately from S, not a module attached to current S hidden layers.
Its residual targets retain preanswer R prediction errors; the auxiliary bootstrap error prior is separately declared.
Acquisition also uses current S probability/Jacobian and coverage, so this is not a faithful reproduction of Learning Loss.
R-to-S image-content alignment and data-selection feedback exist, but alone do not identify a causal RSI gain.
future_design_constraints: If a current-student-conditioned loss observer is pursued, learned loss prediction must be recognized as prior art and considered as an appropriate baseline.
Changing mean loss scale, ranking usefulness, current conditional risk, and reducible learning information are distinct.
Do not use a mean-calibration diagnostic alone to declare acquisition failure or success.
Any project version must derive supervision from actually requested teacher probabilities, not target manual labels.
Preserve adequate same-information KD, fixed seed0, count-matched attribution and the original full primary evaluation before selecting another study.
